To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the southern IBM arc magmas are not in equilibrium with subducted material and (2) the oxygen isotopic data suggest that the subduction component in the southern IBM arc is dominated by sediment melt (<4%).

the oxygen isotopic composition of southern IBM Arc lavas is consistent with a small proportion (mostly <1%) of sediment melt being mixed with mantle peridotites, to form hybrid mantle, which then melts to yield the IBM Arc lavas.

the IBM Arc is not in isotopic equilibrium with the subduction component, and that the oxygen isotopic composition of the subduction zone component is not significantly different from that of mantle peridotite, and that it is probably less depleted in oxygen than previously thought.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the nature and origin of the subduction-related component that is mixed with normal mantle to produce the melts that erupt along convergent margins, and the extent of oxygen exchange between the subduction component and mantle peridotite.
the origin of the subduction components that characterize arc magmas, and the extent to which these components are derived from recycled oceanic lithosphere, and/or from subducted sediment.
the oxygen isotope geochemistry of the Izu-Bonin-Mariana (IBM Arc) and its relationship to the subduction process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxygen isotopic data do not require a large proportion of sediment melt, and do not preclude the possibility of a small proportion.
the IBM Arc is a ‘hybrid’ subduction-related magmatic system, in which the proportion of sediment melt in the subduction zone hybrid is less than 1%.
the IBM Arc melts, and the arc lavas, are derived from a mantle source that has been modified by the addition of a small amount (<4%) of sediment melt.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

oxygen isotopes are not a sensitive tool for identifying subduction components in arc magmas, and that they are not a sensitive tracer of the proportion of subducted material recycled to the mantle, at least at the IBM Arc.
the oxygen isotopic composition of the IBM Arc is not a reliable tracer of the subduction contribution to the arc magmas.
, although the subduction factory is a major component in the production of arc magmas, its contribution to the oxygen isotopic budget of these magmas is minor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen isotopic compositions of IBM Arc magmas do not support the presence of a large, subducted slab-derived fluid component in these magmas.
the oxygen isotopic composition of the IBM Arc lavas is consistent with an origin from the mantle, with little to no contribution from subducted material.
the subduction component is not an oxygen isotopically distinct component, but rather a mixture of mantle peridotite and sediment melt.
